manifest.description: Extract named inherent impl methods into a target submodule file with full module wiring, visibility adjustment, import organization, compile repair, and validation in one compound run.
when_to_use: moving a cluster of methods from one impl block into a child submodule
single-domain extraction from a god-impl (for multi-domain use rust-split-god-impl)
operator has method names in hand and knows the target submodule path
anti_patterns: do not use for multi-partition god-impl splits - use rust-split-god-impl instead
do not use to move top-level items (structs, enums, functions) - use rust-extract-to-submodule
do not use when methods need different visibility from each other - use rust.setVisibility after the move
do not use on non-Rust files

project_dir.description: Absolute path to the Rust project root.

source_file.description: File containing the source impl block, relative to project_dir.

target_file.description: Target submodule file (e.g. src/server/search.rs), relative to project_dir.

impl_name.description: Exact impl name as reported by analysis.implPartition or code.items (for example `impl BlackboxServer`).

method_names.description: Method names to extract from the impl block.

module_name.description: Module name for the mod declaration. Defaults to target_file stem.

visibility.description: Visibility for the mod declaration. Supports `pub` and `pub(crate)`.

target_prelude.description: Prelude for the target file. Defaults to `use super::*;`.

router_name.description: Optional router wrapper name (e.g. `search_tools`) for a #[tool_router] wrapper impl.

router_export_name.description: Optional public helper function name for the router export.

skip_organize_imports.description: Skip the rust.organizeImports step after extraction.

targeted_tests.description: Test names to run after the final cargo check.
